summary.text: A 65-year-old man who had received adjuvant nivolumab for bladder cancer after total cystectomy developed systemic dermatitis as an immune-related adverse event and was hospitalized. On day 16 he was admitted to the ICU for post-cardiac arrest resuscitation because of acute respiratory distress syndrome triggered by aspiration pneumonia. His ventilation had drastically deteriorated with frothy sputum; blood gas showed pH 7.032, PaCO2 86.2 mmHg and PaO2 56.9 mmHg.

Veno-arterial ECMO was introduced because of repeated cardiac arrest due to hypoxia, with a drainage cannula tip advanced to the SVC. One hour later a right IJV reinfusion cannula converted it to V-AV ECMO. A pulmonary artery catheter was placed, muscle relaxation started and the chest X-ray showed white-out under lung rest setting, with PPAO2 300.6 mmHg and PaO2 304.8 mmHg.

After hypoxia improved and cardiac function recovered, the femoral arterial reinfusion cannula was removed 21 h after ECMO induction and the circuit was converted to V-V ECMO. The reinfusion cannula tip was pulled up to the upper RA, and PPAO2 296.3 mmHg and PaO2 268.4 mmHg were measured with almost no lung ventilation. TEE at 45 h with a microbubble test found no clear right-to-left shunt, and the recirculation ratio was 20.0%.

Oxygenation was maintained for 18 h after muscle relaxation was stopped. ECMO was weaned off on ICU day 12, ventilation was weaned and he was extubated on day 13, and CT on day 14 showed thrombus from the right common iliac vein to the femoral vein but not from the SVC to the bilateral IJVs. He had fully recovered and left the ICU on day 24.
